claim: niri's documented security model assumes unsandboxed host programs are trusted: 'Anything with access to niri's IPC socket can, among other things: Spawn a Wayland client' — which in turn can record the screen, emulate input, read the clipboard, spoof password dialogs via layer-shell, and kill/replace lock screens; there is no per-connection authentication on the IPC socket.
stance_target: gap-06: security implications of a fleet agent holding niri IPC access — it is equivalent to full session control
scope_conditions: unsandboxed clients on the host; sandboxed clients must have the IPC socket removed, D-Bus blocked, and a filtered Wayland socket (security-context protocol / Flatpak)
quoted_support: Anything with access to niri's IPC socket can, among other things: Spawn a Wayland client which can do everything in the list above. ... Niri assumes that programs running unsandboxed on the host are trusted.
